findings.title: plotly surface= silently deletes (NaNs) nearly all data points enclosed by their own hull, regardless of surface alpha -- translucent surfaces show no data at all, diverging from matplotlib
findings.description: plotly_backend.py lines 520-539 NaN out every marker point enclosed by that dataset's own surface mesh, as a workaround for plotly's WebGL depth-compositing defect. The code comment justifies it as 'they would be hidden behind the opaque surface anyway', but the hiding is UNCONDITIONAL -- it fires even at surface alpha=0.2, where nothing is opaque. Measured: with surface={'alpha': 0.2} (and identically at the DEFAULT alpha=0.6), dataset 0 keeps 1 of 150 points and dataset 1 keeps 0 of 150. The same call on the matplotlib backend shows all 300 points through the translucent hulls. So the two backends produce fundamentally different plots at the default settings, and the docstring contract is broken twice: (a) the surface docstring's alpha entry explicitly discusses translucent plotly surfaces ('plotly's translucent Mesh3d keeps the full mesh...') with no mention that the DATA disappears beneath them, and (b) keep_points (default True, documented 'if False, hides that dataset's own line/marker') implies True shows the points -- on plotly it effectively does not. Suggested fix direction: only NaN out enclosed points when the surface is (nearly) opaque, e.g. alpha >= ~0.9, or expose the behavior as an explicit option.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
a = rng.normal(size=(150, 3)); b = rng.normal(size=(150, 3)) + np.array([4, 0, 0])
fig = hyp.plot([a, b], '.', surface={'alpha': 0.2}, backend='plotly')
for t in fig.data:
    if t.type == 'scatter3d' and t.x is not None and len(t.x) == 150:
        xs = np.asarray(t.x, dtype=float)
        print(len(xs), int(np.sum(~np.isnan(xs))))  # 150 1 / 150 0

findings.title: density= on coplanar/collinear (constant-column) data silently draws nothing (3D) or a degenerate delta-ridge (2D) -- the docstring-promised UserWarning never fires
findings.description: plot()'s density docstring (plot.py ~1112-1116) promises: 'A dataset with too few points (< 3) or degenerate (singular covariance -- e.g. exactly duplicated/collinear/coplanar points) has its density silently skipped with a UserWarning (never a crash).' The all-identical-points case does warn, but the coplanar/collinear case does not: plot()'s [-1,1] rescale leaves the constant column constant only up to float eps (std ~1.8e-16), so scipy's gaussian_kde no longer raises LinAlgError and fit_kde's degenerate catch (density.py lines 218-225) never triggers. In 3D the near-singular KDE then evaluates to exactly 0.0 at every one of the 50^3 grid points, so iso_surfaces_3d returns [] (density.py lines 411-412, 'if dmax <= 0: return meshes') and NOTHING is drawn, with no warning -- verified against a no-density baseline: identical artist lists. The plotly Volume path has the same silent '(if dmax <= 0: return None)' exit (plotly_backend.py ~1500), verified in PL6. In 2D the near-singular KDE instead yields a quasi-delta ridge with peak density 6.9e7 that IS drawn (no warning). A scientist plotting effectively-2D data embedded in 3D gets no density layer and no explanation.
findings.repro:
import warnings, numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
data = np.column_stack([rng.normal(size=(80, 2)), np.zeros(80)])
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    fig = hyp.plot(data, '.', density=True, reduce=None)
print('warnings:', [str(x.message) for x in w])           # []
ax = fig.axes[0]
print('density artists:', [type(c).__name__ for c in ax.collections])  # cube lines only, no Poly3DCollection

findings.title: plot() docstring documents the plotly 3-D density Volume with stale pre-R2 constants: opacity=min(3.0*alpha, 0.6) and 'a fixed opacityscale ramp' -- code uses min(2.0*alpha, 0.4) and a boost-varying ramp
findings.description: plot.py docstring (~lines 1168-1171) says the plotly 3-D layer uses '`opacity=min(3.0 * alpha, 0.6)`, a fixed `opacityscale` ramp'. The shipped code (density.py resolve_plotly_volume_params, lines 360-361) uses base_opacity = min(2.0 * alpha, 0.4) -- density.py's own comments state the 3.0/0.6 values were 'lowered from the original' in the R2 retune -- and the opacityscale/isomin/pad are NOT fixed: they shift with the auto-boost (isomin 0.05 -> 0.01, breakpoints move with boost t). Verified by real runs: a single (boost=1) dataset gets opacity=0.4 (docstring predicts 0.6), and the standard two-blob scene already gets boosted values (isomin=0.045, opacity=0.64, surface_count=24). The docstring paragraph also never mentions that isomin/opacityscale/pad vary with the small-in-scene boost, though it documents the boost nowhere in the density entry.

findings.title: plot() docstring claims the surface containment rescale 'grows at most 10%'; the code cap is 3.0x (_RESCALE_CAP), deliberately so per meshutil's own docstring
findings.description: plot.py surface docstring, pre_inflate entry (~lines 1079-1085): 'Any shrinkage smoothing introduces is instead recovered by a minimal, mathematically bounded (grow at most 10%) post-hoc rescale...'. meshutil.py sets _RESCALE_CAP = 3.0 (line 303) and _rescale_for_containment's docstring devotes two paragraphs to WHY the cap is 3.0 and not '~1.1 as one might initially expect' (4-point tetrahedra need ~2.9x, 5-point clouds ~2.3x). So the user-facing docstring understates the possible growth by up to 30x of the stated allowance. Related smaller inconsistency: plotly_backend.py line 528 comment says containment 'only targets ~96%+' while meshutil targets target_frac=0.99 (measured on weights: 99.0-99.7% contained).

findings.title: Animated plots drop the per-vertex hue coloring of surfaces: a hue='rainbow' hull renders flat gray when animated, per-vertex-colored when static
findings.description: The QC 2026-07 fix colors a hue'd surface per-vertex (vertex_colors_from_points) in STATIC plots -- verified working on both backends (W5: 1570 unique face RGBs, per-channel spreads unequal [0.613 0.541 0.521]; PL2: 12377 unique vertex colors). But no ANIMATED path passes surface_point_colors: matplotlib_backend.py's animation frames call _mesh_and_draw_3d/_shade_and_cull_3d without it (lines 1011, 1057, 1102, 1171 -- _mesh_and_draw_3d does not even accept the parameter), and plotly_backend.py's _add_animation call (line ~951) does not receive surface_point_colors. Animated surfaces therefore fall back to the flat mean-of-hue color -- for a full rainbow hue that mean is GRAY, which is exactly the 'hull ignores hue' symptom the QC fix addressed. Verified: animate='spin' + continuous hue renders a white/gray hull around rainbow points (rgb channel spreads exactly equal [0.687 0.687 0.687] = grayscale shading of a flat base), while the identical static call renders a hue-tinted hull.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d.art3d import Poly3DCollection
t = np.linspace(0, 4*np.pi, 200)
traj = np.column_stack([np.cos(t), np.sin(t), t/(4*np.pi)])
res = hyp.plot(traj, '.', hue=t, animate='spin', surface={'alpha': 0.5}, return_model=True)
ani = res['animation']; frames = iter(ani.new_frame_seq()); ani._init_draw(); ani._draw_frame(next(frames))
ax = res['fig'].axes[0]
hull = max([c for c in ax.collections if isinstance(c, Poly3DCollection)], key=lambda c: len(c.get_facecolor()))
fc = np.asarray(hull.get_facecolor())[:, :3]
print(np.ptp(fc, axis=0))  # equal channels ~[0.687 0.687 0.687] = flat gray base
findings.expected: Animated surfaces honor hue the same way static ones do (per-vertex blend), or the plot() docstring's animation paragraph documents that hue-following surface colors are static-only.

static W5 spread: [0.613 0.541 0.521] with 1570 unique face RGBs

findings.title: surface= dict VALUES are never validated (unlike density='s exemplary eager validation): bad alpha crashes late and cryptically, pre_inflate=0 leaks a raw QhullError, pre_inflate<0 silently builds an inside-out mesh
findings.description: normalize_surface_arg validates surface KEYS eagerly ('fail fast ... before the expensive analyze/reduce pipeline runs', plot.py comment ~1465) but no VALUES except lighting['lightdir']. Consequences, all verified: (1) surface={'alpha': 1.5} or -0.2 runs the full pipeline then dies inside matplotlib with 'ValueError: RGBA values should be within 0-1 range' -- never mentioning surface['alpha']; alpha='red' dies with 'could not convert string to float: 'red''. Contrast density={'alpha': 1.5} which immediately raises "density['alpha'] must be a real number in (0, 1]; got 1.5". (2) surface={'pre_inflate': 0} collapses the hull to its centroid and crashes with a raw scipy QhullError including a Qhull internals dump ('QH6154 Qhull precision error: Initial simplex is flat...') -- smooth_hull_3d only converts QhullError to ValueError for the initial hull (meshutil.py 235-241); the later ConvexHull(verts) inside _rescale_for_containment (line 490) is unprotected, and build_mesh_3d catches only ValueError (surface.py 235), so the documented 'never a crash' skip path is bypassed. (3) surface={'pre_inflate': -1} silently point-reflects the mesh: 100% of faces end up wound inward (probe: frac outward = 0.000), inverting the Blinn-Phong shading and backface culling. (4) smoothing has no upper bound (face count 4**smoothing; smoothing=5 -> 32768 faces verified; larger values are an unguarded memory/time footgun). Suggested: validate alpha in [0,1], pre_inflate > 0, smoothing int in [0, ~6] in _validate_surface_dict, mirroring _validate_density_values.
findings.expected: Eager ValueErrors naming the key, constraint, and received value -- exactly like density['alpha'|'grid'|'levels'|'per_group'] -- before the pipeline runs; no raw QhullError, no silent inside-out geometry.

findings.title: hypertools.plot the FUNCTION shadows the hypertools.plot subpackage: 'import hypertools.plot.meshutil as m' fails with a cryptic ImportError after 'import hypertools'
findings.description: hypertools/__init__.py binds the name 'plot' to the plot() function, shadowing the plot subpackage as an attribute of the hypertools module. Python's 'import a.b.c as m' binds via attribute traversal, so once hypertools is imported, 'import hypertools.plot.meshutil as m' (or .density/.surface/any hypertools.plot.* module) raises "ImportError: cannot import name 'meshutil' from 'plot' (unknown location)" -- the 'plot' in the message is the FUNCTION's __name__, maximally confusing. The same statement works in a fresh interpreter where hypertools was not yet imported, making the failure appear nondeterministic. 'from hypertools.plot import meshutil' and plain 'import hypertools.plot.meshutil' (no as) always work. This is the scipy-style name-collision wart; worth either a rename note in docs or an __init__ that re-exposes the subpackage under an alias.
findings.repro:
python -c "
import hypertools
print(type(hypertools.plot))            # <class 'function'>
import hypertools.plot.meshutil          # works
import hypertools.plot.meshutil as m     # ImportError
"
findings.expected: All standard import forms of a public module work, or the limitation is documented.
findings.actual:
type(hypertools.plot): <class 'function'>
plain dotted import ok
as-form ImportError: cannot import name 'meshutil' from 'plot' (unknown location)
docs_impact: docs (any page that shows hypertools.plot.* imports)

findings.title: numpy bools rejected for surface=/density= top-level (density=np.True_ -> ValueError) while the per_group dict VALUE explicitly accepts np.bool_ -- inconsistent
findings.description: normalize_density_arg/normalize_surface_arg test 'density is True' / 'is False', so np.True_/np.False_ (which arise naturally from numpy expressions, e.g. flags stored in arrays) are rejected with "density must be None, a bool, or a dict; got np.True_" even though the message says 'a bool' and numpy bools behave as bools everywhere else in the API -- including density['per_group'], whose validator explicitly allows np.bool_ (density.py line 149: isinstance(per_group, (bool, np.bool_))). Either accept np.bool_ at the top level (isinstance check) or say 'a Python bool' in the message.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
blob = np.random.default_rng(3).normal(size=(50, 3))
hyp.plot(blob, '.', density=np.True_)  # ValueError: density must be None, a bool, or a dict; got np.True_
findings.expected: np.True_/np.False_ treated as True/False (matching per_group's tolerance), or an error message that says a Python bool is required.
findings.actual:
E14a: ValueError: density must be None, a bool, or a dict; got np.True_
E14b: ValueError: surface must be None, a bool, a dict, or a list of bool/dict; got np.True_
